title: The Silver Spire
aliases: Fenwick’s Wizarding Clock Tower of Eovar
Silver Spire Public Baths, Arcane Market & Healing House
type: Wizarding tower · public baths & healing house
dek: Fenwick’s Wizarding Clock Tower of Eovar grows into the Silver Spire: public baths, healing, shelter and an arcane market beneath his private magical rooms.

facts.Public services: Baths · healing · arcane market · food & shelter
facts.Layout: Four floors · public rooms below, private rooms above
facts.Chronology: Bounty board recorded by February 2025; opening dates unknown

sources: Tower public notice · edited 21 July 2025; original post 13 January 2025 · https://discord.com/channels/1177270231513694249/1328364550084362350/1328370733474381837

body:
The Silver Spire begins as Fenwick d’Jorasco’s wizarding tower in Eovar Harbor. Its lower floors welcome the city; its upper rooms shelter staff, supplies and private magical work. It later takes the civic name Silver Spire Public Baths, Arcane Market & Healing House, making care for Eovar part of the building’s standing purpose.

Inside the clock tower

The plan shows a gradual passage from public space to increasingly secure rooms. The first three levels have spiral stairs; the fourth is reached through a ceiling trapdoor, with levitation specified in the plan.

Why build in Eovar?

Fenwick chooses Eovar after helping its infirmary and seeing the scale of its needs. He describes long neglect, underinvestment, decaying grandeur and a Thieves Guild so entrenched that ordinary residents have learned to coexist with it. Compared with Pristinia, he finds the harbor poorly supported.

His aim is to give the people hope through something useful and lasting. Tobias Goodbarrel helps turn that intention into a building: Fenwick praises his work during an early tour and later trusts him to house-sit while he is away.

First floor · baths, welcome and refuge

A small entry leads into a lecture or waiting room with public seating and two private bathing rooms. Fenwick plans a reservoir filled by a Decanter of Endless Water, with bathing scheduled in private periods and offered free of charge.

The baths support the Eovar Infirmary. Lionel Therran recognizes how clean water and sanitation could help patients whose wounds would otherwise become infected. Fenwick also envisions food distribution, temporary shelter, medical overflow and a protected refuge overseen by a manager and a small guard presence.

Ordinary residents can enter without being adventurers. The first floor puts clean water, rest and care at the base of a powerful wizard’s home.

Second floor · staff, guards and ravens

The balcony opens onto a common room with a work table, desk, raven cages, weapon rack and equipment storage. Three bunk beds provide sleeping places for six staff or guards. This level buffers the public rooms from the private tower above.

Fenwick proposes a raven delivery network with the Ale-Chemy Knights: trained birds would carry messages between settlements, with Sending available for the final leg when needed. He hopes it can eventually extend across Prima. The cages and intended service belong to the tower’s design; the full island-wide network is not established as completed.

Third floor · flexible rooms and secure storage

Two small private bedrooms and storage surround an open central room. Lionel suggests a staging area, map room or war room for adventurers preparing operations. Fenwick initially keeps the space flexible rather than fixing its use.

Discussion of a prison cell exposes a more alarming possibility. Fenwick proposes using Flesh to Stone to secure dangerous prisoners, then restoring them when needed. He reasons that petrification might protect them and pause disease. This is a proposal, not a documented use of the tower as a prison, and it reveals how far his medically practical reasoning can carry him.

Fourth floor · Fenwick’s private magical work

Bookcases, scroll cases, maps and research space occupy the wizard’s private level. Fenwick discusses removing the construction ladder and controlling access through magical movement; the floor plan labels a trapdoor with no stairs and a need to levitate.

Later he casts Simulacrum here, using the fourth floor for prolonged work that requires privacy. Public service below coexists with the secure home and considerable power of the wizard above.

An evening for Eovar’s families

During cold, miserable fog, Fenwick notices children trapped indoors and exhausted parents. He asks Robben at the infirmary to spread the word, and the tower’s first floor fills with children, parents and grandparents.

He opens the bathing rooms for restroom use, distributes food and rations, and conjures an illusionary reenactment of a recent battle. The monsters become less frightening, the heroes suitably heroic, and Fenwick answers questions and makes the children laugh. The public room becomes a warm gathering place through the simple choice to open it.

A lantern always lit

A later public notice formalizes the Silver Spire’s services: restorative private baths, medical and magical care coordinated with the Eovar Infirmary, an arcane market for potions, scrolls, spells and magical supplies, and continued food and shelter for neighbors in need.

The Healing House is meant to absorb overflow and coordinate triage while supporting Eovar’s existing healers. The notice promises that lack of money or status alone will not turn someone away.

“A Lantern Always Lit.”

The Silver Spire · public notice

Fenwick signs the notice as Fenwick d’Jorasco, Citizen of Eovar. His identity has moved from helping the city to belonging to it.

“We are Eovar.”

At a celebration connected with opening the baths, Fenwick tells the gathered people that he loves Eovar’s people. He describes mutual care, shared building and a promise that nobody should be forgotten. He rejects a pattern of adventurers arriving, creating trouble and leaving ordinary residents with the consequences.

At a later public opening, he presents the Spire as one of the first stones in Eovar’s reconstruction. His wider ambitions include sewers, public health, food security, docks, streets, walls, markets, communications and regional trade. These are civic goals, not proof that every project has been completed.

He wants a city able to feed, guard and heal its own people, with autonomy from the Rahu, Pristinia, thieves and dependence on visiting heroes. The tower gives that ambition a place where neighbors can receive practical help.

Public work and the tower’s chronology

By February 2025, Tobias directs newcomers to the tower’s notice board for open material bounties. Alongside baths and care, it offers a repeatable way to find work and enter Eovar’s economy.

The construction tours, family gathering, bathing-room celebration and later public opening have no settled dates. The tower’s exact position on Eovar’s map also remains unconfirmed; the interior plan establishes its rooms without fixing that external location.

The opening notice and its date

The surviving notice names the Silver Spire Public Baths, Arcane Market and Healing House and advertises service to Eovar. The post began in January 2025, but its text explicitly records an edit on 21 July. The named facilities and public-service claim belong to the surviving edited notice. Its original timestamp cannot securely date the Silver Spire name, opening or every advertised service to January.

Building, watching and the unfinished rookery

Tobias begins preparing Fenwick’s chosen lot in Eovar, then records successive days of work. These short entries place the building effort before the later tours and public notices; they do not supply a single secure opening date.

When Fenwick is away, Tobias describes himself as tower-watching and later says he will spend the night there. The Spire depends on another person’s presence as well as its founder’s plans. This temporary responsibility does not establish a transfer of ownership.

Later Tobias tells Coralyn that Fenwick has built space for a rookery and is trying to train birds to carry messages between towns. That report fits the cages and proposed service in the floor plan while keeping the larger network unfinished. The surviving edited opening notice remains a separate dating question.
